item.title: Hope Café — Fri Sep 25, 6:30 PM — International House (I-House)
item.description:
Come celebrate the end of summer and the start of fall with an evening designed to build connection and community. Hope Café is a little bit workshop, a little bit party — a warm, welcoming space where live music, creative activities, and guided conversations invite you to pause, reconnect, and feel like you belong. All you need to do is show up with a curious mind and an open heart. What to Expect: Doors open at 6:30 PM with live world jazz by Nick Carvajal and Jim Frink. Local vendors Jumi Shrub, Enamora Empanadas, and Upper Crust Baking will have snacks and drinks available. Community story sharing and playful creative exercises continue through 8:30 PM, after which guests are encouraged to linger and connect. Sliding Scale: $15-$25
Source: The Dirt

item.title: An Evening with Tyler Merritt — Fri Sep 25, 7:00 PM — Davis Veterans Memorial Theatre
item.description: Join Tyler for an amazing evening of connection that will encourage your heart and remind you that Hope really does change everything HOPE: This Changes Everything Tour An Evening with Tyler Merritt What if hope isn’t something you wait for… but something you choose? In a time when division feels louder than connection and fear often overshadows possibility, Hope: This Changes Everything offers something different—an evening that will make you laugh, reflect, and leave believing that even small acts of hope can change the world around us. Join bestselling author, actor, activist, and beloved storyteller Tyler Merritt for a one-of-a-kind live experience filled with unforgettable stories, humor, music, heartfelt conversation, and practical encouragement. With his signature authenticity, Tyler invites audiences to rediscover what connects us, challenges us, and ultimately gives us reason to hope. Whether you’re navigating a difficult season, looking for inspiration, or simply longing

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Fri Sep 25, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Hunter, Bran, & Brown Live — Fri Sep 25, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Join Laurin Hunter, Brandon “someguyBran” Dominguez and David J. Brown for an evening of original music, storytelling and collaboration. Blending influences that span jazz, folk, Americana, pop, rock, soul and beyond, each artist brings a distinct musical voice while sharing a passion for authentic live performance. Together, they’ll present an evening of original songs, fresh interpretations of timeless classics, creativity and connection where every performance offers something unique.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Oct 14, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Author Event: Jon Else — Thu Sep 24, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader
item.description: Jon Else @ The Avid Reader Thursday Sep 24th, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – Frenchman Flat: The Rise and Fall of Atomic Bombs The story of a single nuclear bomb’s deep origins, brief life during the Cold War, and lasting environmental and political legacies—as a fresh path to consider the entire sweep of the American nuclear enterprise. A grave reminder of the frightening truth about nuclear testing, as international norms waver. As the US and Russia let one treaty after another falter and expire, this urgent book reminds us of the price of those tests. Frenchman Flat recounts the science, politics, and human experience of those who developed nuclear weapons, suffered the consequences, and fought for and against arms control between the 1940s and 1990s. The throughline of this vast, complex story is a 37-kiloton atomic bomb dubbed “Priscilla” that was exploded above a custom-built mini-civilization at Frenchman Flat, Nevada, in 1957. item.title: Let’s Talk Murder! Mystery Authors Discuss Their Work — Thu Sep 24, 7:00 PM — Winters Community Library
item.description: From cozy village mysteries to dark psychological thrillers, mystery novels are perennially popular: studied by academics, promoted by celebrities, and discussed in book clubs worldwide. What is the draw of these stories, combining logical deduction and atmospheric dread? Winters Friends of the Library invites everyone to learn more at a special author talk with three award-winning mystery writers. Catriona McPherson, Jennifer K. Morita, and Laura Jensen Walker will share insights on their writing lives and the mystery genre. Whether you are an avid mystery reader or new to the genre, it will be fascinating to hear what these authors have to say about the challenges and pleasures of writing mysterious fiction. Following the talk, attendees may enjoy refreshments and chat with the authors and fellow readers. Books will be available for purchase and signing. There is no charge for the event, but donations to support library programs will be gratefully accepted. For more information, v

item.description:
The first three years in a child’s life are an amazing time of growth that fill parents and caregivers with awe and wonder. Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

item.title: Workshop: Organize, Cite, Publish: Citation Management from First Search to Final Draft — Fri Oct 30, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Keep your sources, notes, PDFs, and citations organized from your first search through your final draft. In this workshop, we'll explore strategies for managing research throughout the literature review and publication process using citation management tools. Discover efficient ways to import, organize and tag sources, annotate PDFs, and generate citations and bibliographies. Come learn the tools and workflows that can save you time—and make your thesis advisor a little envious.
Register:
Zoom Registration
In-Person Registration
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Workshop: Mastering Your Literature Search: Techniques, Tools and AI — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
This workshop is ideal for any student or researcher embarking on a literature search or review, or anyone wanting to learn about emerging AI tools for literature searching. The session will cover (1) how to translate your research question into a search strategy that will uncover the scholarly literature you need, (2) the library tools you will need for your searches, and (3) an introduction to the AI tools designed for literature searching and how they can supplement your search strategy.
Register:
Zoom Registration
In-Person Registration
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Workshop: So you’re ready to publish your first scientific paper?... — Fri Nov 13, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Publishing research in a scientific journal is a critical step in every researcher's journey. However, it can be a very complex and intimidating landscape when doing it for the first time. This workshop will provide an introduction to major parts of the process including, an overview of the scientific publishing landscape, selecting a journal, working with collaborators, and more! This workshop is aimed at all STEM-aligned fields and all experience levels, but beginners are especially welcome.
